summary: A governance framework for frontier AI models covering risk assessment and mitigation across cyber offense, CBRN risks, harmful manipulation, and loss of control. Maps internal safety practices to emerging regulations including EU AI Act and California transparency laws.

risk_tiers.description: Models assessed to pose critical risks that cannot be adequately mitigated. Deployment is halted pending additional safeguards.
criteria: Model demonstrates capability for autonomous CBRN weapon development
Model shows potential for loss of human control
Model can autonomously conduct sophisticated cyber attacks
Risk mitigation measures are insufficient for identified threats

risk_tiers.description: Models with significant capability in sensitive domains requiring comprehensive safety measures, monitoring, and restricted access.
criteria: Model has significant cyber offense capabilities
Model can generate CBRN-relevant technical information
Model demonstrates capacity for harmful manipulation at scale
Model requires extensive safety testing before deployment

risk_tiers.description: Models with moderate capabilities that require standard safety measures and monitoring but can be deployed with appropriate guardrails.
criteria: Model has general-purpose capabilities without extreme risk
Standard content filtering addresses primary risks
Model operates within well-understood capability boundaries
Existing safety measures provide adequate protection

risk_tiers.description: Models with limited capabilities posing minimal novel risks beyond existing technology.
criteria: Model capabilities well within established safety boundaries
No significant uplift in dangerous capabilities identified

key_obligations.obligation: Conduct systematic risk assessments evaluating model capabilities in cyber offense, CBRN, harmful manipulation, and autonomous action domains before deployment
Implement model reporting including capability evaluations, safety testing results, and known limitations disclosed to regulators and downstream users
Maintain security risk management program protecting model weights, training infrastructure, and deployment systems against theft or unauthorized access
Establish incident response procedures for safety-relevant events including detection, escalation, mitigation, and post-incident review processes
Incorporate external expert input through red-teaming, safety advisory boards, and third-party audits to validate safety assessments

enforcement_timeline: Published May 29, 2026. Aligns with EU AI Act requirements for general-purpose AI providers and California transparency laws. Continuously updated as capabilities and regulations evolve.
recent_changes: Maps to EU AI Act GPAI provider obligations and California SB-1047 requirements
Covers frontier model risks: cyber, CBRN, manipulation, loss of control
